7.text: Along the western parts of the Arctic shores of the Old World there

8.text: dwell a number of tribes who have possessed from ancient times domesticated

9.text: reindeer that are harnessed to sledges and also used for food. Their herds

10.text: are, or rather were, large; and their whole existence is based on the supply

16.text: The widespread branches of the Tungus and Lamut constitute the most

17.text: prominent reindeer tribe of eastern Siberia. Usually they live some distance

18.text: from the shore, and many bands use the saddle in place of the sledge. Their

19.text: herds are so small that they can use their reindeer for riding and transportation

20.text: only, not for slaughter. They have not become nomadic, but, owing to the

21.text: introduction of the reindeer, have been enabled to extend their hunting and

22.text: fishing expeditions over a larger extent of territory, in the same way as the

23.text: North American Indians did after the introduction of horses. Several bands,

24.text: however, raise large herds, so that they are able to live on their products.

25.text: Although the riding of reindeer is the most striking feature among Tungus

26.text: reindeer-breeders, numerous bands have adopted a peculiar form of sledge

27.text: (Fig. 4) with stanchions fitted into circular holes in the runners and fastened

28.text: with thongs, and with a circular bow-like fore-part for attaching the traces, —

29.text: the same as is used throughout eastern Siberia for dog-teams.
